title: Exercise-released fat-burning molecule boosts muscle strength, reduces fatigue
content:
Researchers discovered that a naturally occurring molecule released during exercise helps muscles become stronger, resist fatigue, and withstand damage.  

The molecule is already available as a dietary supplement and could open new avenues for treating muscle deterioration associated with type 2 diabetes.
summary: Researchers discovered that a naturally occurring molecule released during exercise helps muscles become stronger, resist fatigue, and withstand damage. The molecule, already available as a dietary supplement, could open new avenues for treating muscle deterioration associated with type 2 diabetes.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find two opposite microscopic spirals inside narwhal tusk
content: The narwhal’s iconic spiral tusk—historically prized in Europe as a unicorn’s horn—has been shown to embody a striking natural engineering feature. Advanced X‑ray imaging by an international team of scientists revealed that the tusk houses two microscopic spirals intertwined and twisting in opposite directions.
summary: The narwhal’s spiral tusk, historically prized in Europe as a unicorn horn, hides a natural engineering marvel. Advanced X‑ray imaging by an international team revealed the tusk contains two intertwined microscopic spirals that twist in opposite directions.
author: Science Daily

title: Harvard team creates microscopic chip that emits 120× more UV light
content: Harvard‑led researchers have developed a microscopic device that generates 120 times more ultraviolet light than previous comparable approaches by efficiently converting red light into UV. The breakthrough could unlock smaller quantum computers, ultra‑precise atomic clocks, and compact environmental sensors.
summary: Harvard‑led researchers have developed a microscopic device that generates 120 times more ultraviolet light than previous comparable approaches by efficiently converting red light into UV. The breakthrough could enable smaller quantum computers, ultra‑precise atomic clocks and compact environmental sensors.

title: Russia may plan satellite launch carrying nuclear weapon, experts discuss effects
content: Reports suggest Russia may be planning to launch a satellite carrying a nuclear weapon. In a video, Science Editor Ian Sample asks Madeleine Finlay how a nuclear detonation in space would impact people on Earth.

title: Landsat 9 captures cloud‑shrouded Shivelyuch volcano amid ongoing eruptions
content:
Shivelyuch, also known as Shiveluch, is a volcano on Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula that is noted for frequent eruptions and persistent cloud cover. A recent image from the Operational Land Imager (OLI) aboard Landsat 9, taken on November 8 2026, shows the snowy peak obscured by clouds that hover beneath its 3,283‑meter (10,771‑foot) summit. The clouds do not blanket the volcano’s caldera or its northern upper slopes, leaving a clear view of those areas.

The volcano’s upper reaches contain a caldera that measures 9 kilometers (5.6 miles) across and opens to the south. Within the caldera a dark lava dome is visible, formed by vents that extrude viscous magma. Lava domes at Shivelyuch undergo cycles of growth and collapse, and when they collapse they can trigger fast‑moving avalanches of hot ash and rock known as pyroclastic flows.

According to the Kamchatka Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT), effusive eruptions of lava and explosive activity had been occurring at Shivelyuch for months as of November 2026. Satellites routinely detect thermal anomalies from the volcano, and on the day the image was captured KVERT reported a plume of resuspended ash drifting 120 kilometers (75 miles) eastward. This level of activity is described as relatively tame for the mountain.

Explosive eruptions from Shivelyuch periodically loft ash several kilometers into the atmosphere, allowing it to travel great distances and pose risks to aircraft. In July 2026, an ash plume rode the jet stream over the Bering Sea into Alaskan airspace, prompting the cancellation of multiple flights, according to news reports.

The Earth Observatory image was produced by Lauren Dauphin using Landsat data from the U. S. Geological Survey, and the accompanying story was written by Lindsey Doermann. The image and story are part of NASA Earth Observatory’s “Image of the Day” series.
summary: Landsat 9 captures cloud‑shrouded Shivelyuch volcano amid ongoing eruptions.

Easy to spot in twilight skies above fields, fences, backyards, and even stone walls, the Moon was big and bright, and at its full phase. title: Avi Davidson becomes first trial participant to use nerve‑connected prosthetic hand at home
content: Over the last few weeks, I’ve been talking to Alexander (Avi) Davidson. There are a lot of remarkable things about Avi. He sustained a horrific injury as a teenager, which left him paralyzed and without a left hand. Today, he uses his own experience to guide his practice as a trauma therapist. He’s also taking part in a clinical trial of some new tech that allows him to move—and feel with—a prosthetic hand. Unlike standard prosthetics, this one connects directly to nerves in Avi’s arm. He literally has wires coming out of his arm to plug it in with. Avi’s the ninth person to trial this tech. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently, for things like drinking from a cup (which is not easy ) and writing (also not easy ). What struck me the most over our conversations was Avi’s outlook and approach to not just his injuries and learning to use this cutting-edge technology, but to life itself. He has learned how to use something like seven different prosthetics in the 17 years since his accident. By taking part in this trial, he’s had to fit hundreds of hours of lab-based training and physical therapy around his demanding job. He had surgery to implant electrodes in his arm and will eventually need another to remove them. And he won’t even get to keep the latest prosthetic long term. “While it’s unfortunate at times, and irritating at times, I do not regret what has come from [the accident], or the fact that it happened,” he told me. “I am not going to benefit from this … I wanted to be a part of this in the context of being able to help push the technology forward.” The research team at the University of Utah that is running the trial hopes it will answer longstanding questions about the technology. How does it fare in a real-world setting, outside of the lab? What do people end up using it for? Where can improvements be made? There may be some surprises along the way. Avi has found that his prosthetic wrist can feel sore and stiff when it’s been overused, just like his flesh-and-blood wrist. Weirdly, that feeling can be relieved by stretching it out. What’s going on here? No one really knows. Scientists don’t know whether Avi’s brain will change as a result of using the bionic hand, either. Before the trial started, they performed brain scans to see how his missing left hand was represented in his brain. Will that change? And what might that mean for people who are born without limbs—how might a bionic limb affect their brains? Avi will have the device until late January 2027 at the least, and potentially for another year. After that? Again, no one knows. It will depend on how the research is progressing, how Avi feels, and how much funding the team can secure. As a result, it’s not clear how long the device might even be expected to last in a person’s body. I’ll be following this study, though, and will keep you posted. This article first appeared in The Checkup, MIT Technology Review’s weekly biotech newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Thursday, and read articles like this first, sign up here.
summary: Over the last few weeks, I’ve been talking to Alexander (Avi) Davidson. There are a lot of remarkable things about Avi.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: MIT Technology Review Opens 2027 Innovators Under 35 Competition
content:
MIT Technology Review has opened the nomination window for its 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition. The editors will annually select 35 young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors who have made significant contributions to fields such as human disease, climate change, and other pressing societal challenges.  

Candidates must be under 35 years old as of October 1, 2027, meaning they must have been born on or after October 2, 1992. Nominations can be submitted for individuals anywhere in the world who have produced a major finding or advance and can demonstrate real‑world impact. The nomination process is free and takes only a few minutes; nominations must be received by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, January 19.  

After the deadline, MIT Technology Review editors will review all nominees and select a group of semifinalists. Those semifinalists will be invited to submit a formal application, after which a panel of expert judges will evaluate the applicants and determine the finalists. More details about the selection process are available on the review’s website.  

The Innovators Under 35 list began in 1999 and has become an annual exercise that helps the review’s reporters identify the brightest young minds in the fields they cover. Subscribers can view the 2026 list and explore the full archives. The review looks forward to receiving nominations for the 2027 class.
summary: Every year, the editors at MIT Technology Review select 35 of the world’s top young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors to honor as our newest class of Innovators Under 35. And starting today, our 2027 competition is officially open for nominations.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: MIT Technology Review opens Innovators Under 35 nominations; bionic hand trial probes brain
content:
The MIT Technology Review has announced that the 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open for nominations. Each year the review selects 35 of the world’s brightest young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors for its Innovators Under 35 list. The 2027 edition seeks researchers and founders who are engineering solutions to society’s most formidable problems, from human disease to climate change, as well as those who have made clever and useful inventions, important new scientific discoveries, or technological breakthroughs early in their careers. Nominees may be based anywhere in the world but must be under 35 on October 1, 2027. The newsletter provides instructions on how to submit a nomination.

The same edition of The Download also highlights a story from The Checkup, the weekly biotech newsletter, about a bionic hand that could offer new insights into the human mind. The story follows Avi Davidson, who suffered a horrific injury as a teenager that left him paralyzed and without a left hand. Davidson now works as a trauma therapist and is participating in a clinical trial of new technology that allows him to move—and feel—with a prosthetic hand. Prior to the trial, researchers scanned his brain to examine how the missing left hand was represented in his neural circuitry and to assess whether that representation might change with the use of the prosthetic. The article discusses what a bionic hand might reveal about the mind and what the findings could mean for people born without limbs.

Both pieces appear in the same daily edition of The Download, which is described as a weekday newsletter that delivers a daily dose of what’s happening in technology. The Innovators Under 35 announcement and the bionic‑hand story are presented as separate items within the newsletter, each linked to its source—MIT Technology Review for the competition and The Checkup for the prosthetic‑hand feature.
summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Our 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open Every year, MIT Technology Review honors 35 of the world’s brightest young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors in our Innovators Under 35 list.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Americans Create Repair Cafés in Churches and Warehouses to Combat Throwaway Culture
content: Americans are establishing Repair Cafés in church basements and warehouses, creating cozy yet radical spaces where neighbors gather to help one another repair broken items instead of discarding them, thereby confronting a throwaway culture.
summary: Americans are building cozy yet radical spaces in church basements and warehouses. These spaces encourage people to fix broken items instead of throwing them away.

content:

The current listings show a price of $249 at Amazon and $249.99 at Best Buy, down from $349.99.

title: Apple Watch SE 3 discounted to $179 (40mm) and $209 (44mm) for Black Friday
content:
During Black Friday the Apple Watch SE 3 is being offered at reduced prices. The 40 mm GPS model is listed at roughly $179 on Amazon, Walmart and Target, a $70 discount that is $20 lower than its prior lowest price. The 44 mm GPS version is priced around $209 at the same retailers, also $70 off and $20 beneath its earlier low point.

The SE 3, launched more than a year ago, adds an always‑on display to Apple’s budget‑friendly wearable line. It shares several features with higher‑end models such as the Series 12, including double‑tap and wrist‑flick gestures, fast charging and on‑device Siri. The watch does not include advanced health sensors like blood‑oxygen monitoring or an electrocardiogram, and its battery life is modest compared with premium models. Because of its feature set and the current discounts, the SE 3 is recommended as the Apple Watch most people should consider buying on Black Friday.

title: Sony, LG, and TCL TVs Over 50% Off for Black Friday
content:
Black Friday sales have arrived, offering significant discounts on televisions from major manufacturers including Sony, LG, TCL, Vizio, Hisense, Samsung, and Roku. The article highlights that while TVs are substantial purchases that can last for years, the current sales make it an opportune time to upgrade. Recommendations span various technologies, including RGB LED, OLED, and Mini LED, with the assertion that the featured models provide value commensurate with their reduced prices.

TCL’s flagship X11L SQD-Mini LED TV, described as the best TV the company has ever built, is available at steep discounts. Originally priced near $3,000 for the 75-inch model, it is now listed at $2,997.99 at Amazon. Larger 85-inch and 98-inch versions are discounted at Best Buy and Amazon, respectively. The article notes that the X11L offers blazing brightness and great color accuracy. Additionally, the TCL QM8L, which utilizes the same SQD technology for higher brightness and color but at a lower cost, is discounted significantly, with the 65-inch model dropping from $2,499.99 to $997.99 at Amazon.

LG’s B6E OLED TV, an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, is featured for its four HDMI 2.1 ports, 120Hz refresh rate, and pixel-perfect contrast. While lower brightness is noted as a compromise for the cheaper OLED, the 55-inch model is discounted from $1,399.99 to $699.99 at Best Buy. Sony’s Bravia 7 II, the company’s first RGB LED TV, is also heavily discounted. Despite a slightly reflective screen, it is praised for its picture quality and processing, with the 55-inch model reduced from $2,099.99 to $1,199.99 at Best Buy.

Other notable deals include the Vizio Mini LED Quantum 4K TV, which is highlighted for its privacy features and ease of use as a "dumb" TV, with the 50-inch model dropping to $198 at Walmart. Hisense offers discounts on both its 2026 CanvasTV, a 4K QLED model with a matte display and 144Hz variable refresh rate, and the U7SG mini-LED TV, which is noted for its brightness and reflection handling. The 55-inch CanvasTV is available for $697.99 at Amazon, while the 55-inch U7SG is listed at $599.99 at Best Buy.

Samsung’s S95H OLED, a winner of Value Electronics’ TV Shootout, features a glare-free screen and excellent color accuracy. Prices for the 55-inch model have fallen from $2,499.99 to $1,899.99 at Best Buy. Finally, Roku’s Pro Series 4K OLED TV is presented as an affordable option for gamers and movie enthusiasts, with the 55-inch model discounted from $999.99 to $699.99 at Amazon. The article suggests that these Black Friday offers provide a wide range of options for consumers seeking high-quality displays at reduced costs.
summary: Black Friday sales feature discounted prices on several Sony, LG, and TCL TVs, many of which are over 50% off their original prices. The article lists specific models such as TCL X11L, LG B6E OLED, Sony Bravia 7 II, and others, along with their reduced prices and key features.

title: Grand Theft Auto VI features unique ending due to its couple-focused storyline
content:
Most Grand Theft Auto titles, like many open‑world games, let players continue exploring the map after the credits finish. The main story is treated as one segment of a larger, ongoing experience, with locations and side missions often remaining unvisited.

Grand Theft Auto VI departs from that pattern. According to producer Rob Nelson, the game’s narrative follows a couple who are trying to leave the criminal world permanently. Because the story’s focus is on that final break from crime, an open‑ended post‑credit world “didn’t make sense,” Nelson explained.

Consequently, GTA VI delivers an ending that aligns with its plot rather than preserving the usual open‑world continuation found in previous entries. This design choice reflects the game’s distinct storytelling approach.
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI does not leave its world open after the credits like previous entries, because its story follows a couple trying to leave a criminal life. Producer Rob Nelson said that type of ending did not make sense for this game.
author: The Verge

title: Oura Ring 5 drops to $299 for Black Friday, its biggest discount yet
content:
The Oura Ring 5 has slashed its price for Black Friday, dropping to an all‑time low of $299 on Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Oura’s own online store. The discount is $100 off the ring’s regular $399 price and is the largest markdown the product has seen.

Compared with the Ring 4, the new model is thinner, lighter, and more durable, making it more comfortable to wear during the day and while sleeping. It tracks sleep, activity, heart rate, and other health metrics just like its predecessor and offers roughly the same battery life and sensor set. The Ring 5’s charging case now supports wireless charging, though the case is sold separately for $99.

Oura has added several software features to the Ring 5. Health Radar monitors for significant changes in health, and users can import medical lab results, track GLP‑1 medications, and receive AI‑assisted medical guidance through a partnership with Counsel Health. A colleague, Victoria Song, noted that the Counsel Health feature makes it easier to connect with a doctor for quick medical questions, though it may not suit more serious concerns.

To access most health insights, users must maintain a $5.99 monthly Oura membership. Because the Ring 5 and Ring 4 are similar, Oura advises existing Ring 4 owners not to upgrade. However, for those new to smart rings, the Black Friday discount makes the Ring 5 an attractive option, only $50 more than the Ring 4’s starting price.
summary: The Oura Ring 5 is now priced at $299, a $100 discount, at Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Oura’s online store for Black Friday. The Ring 5 is thinner, lighter and more comfortable than the Ring 4 while offering similar health‑tracking features and battery life.
author: The Verge

title: Volvo lets drivers test updated 2028 XC60 and XC90 plug‑in hybrids with bigger batteries
content:
Volvo arranged travel and accommodation for Ars to drive its updated plug‑in hybrids, the XC60 and XC90. The Swedish automaker provided flights from Washington, DC, to Copenhagen, Denmark, and lodging so that Ars could test the vehicles. Ars notes that it does not accept paid editorial content.

Volvo’s product planners had originally envisioned the XC90, launched in 2015, and the smaller XC60, introduced in 2017, as the final models of their kind as electrification progressed. The anticipated shift to all‑electric vehicles, however, has not occurred as expected, particularly in the United States. Meanwhile, Europe and China continue to electrify, raising questions about investing in new replacements for models that may not have an eight‑year lifespan in many markets.

Instead of developing entirely new vehicles, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 a lifecycle refresh.
summary: Volvo provided flights from Washington, DC, to Copenhagen, Denmark, and accommodation so Ars could drive the XC60 and XC90 plug‑in hybrids. The 2028 refresh adds a much larger battery to the PHEVs along with updated infotainment and interior features.
author: Ars Technica

title: Ars staff share holiday gift picks for 2026, featuring books, bikes and gadgets
content: The holiday shopping season is upon us, and as is our custom, we're here with a list of Ars staffers' favorite recent purchases that could make good gifts. (Or maybe they might be a gift you get yourself!) Rather than try to write a definitive "best gifts for your sister or brother" type of guide, we simply polled Ars staffers on stuff they've actually bought this year that they recommend. The thinking is that if we're into it, hopefully some of you or your friends or family might be. As such, there's no rhyme or reason to these selections, really; it's just a list of stuff we bought that we're happy about. It's heavy on interesting books and cycling accessories, but there are some gadgets and the like in here, too. For each gadget (or whatever else it might be), we have a brief description of how or why we’ve been using this particular thing and why we would recommend it. Our picks are ordered by price, from lowest to highest. Note, though, that the prices of these products are listed as they were when the list was written. Online retailers often adjust prices frequently, especially around Black Friday, so just a heads up: The price might be different by the time you read this. Read full article Comments
summary: Ars staff compiled a list of their recent purchases to suggest holiday gifts for 2026. The selections, which range from books and cycling accessories to various gadgets, are presented in order of price with a disclaimer that listed prices may change.
author: Ars Technica

title: Intel pressured by Trump administration to give 10% stake or face unknown consequences
content: The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company. Right now. Or else. Do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.” Shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.” Read full article Comments
summary: The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company. Right now.
author: Ars Technica

title: Independent developers craft GTA‑style games set in their own cities
content:
Independent game developers across Europe are adapting the open‑world, crime‑focused style popularized by Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto series to their own cities, from Helsinki to Istanbul, and doing so without the large budgets of major studios. The developers say they can place the series’ 3D template in any location that has people and enough cars to create the familiar chaos.

One example highlighted is Eamonn Swayah, who imagined a version of the original Grand Theft Auto set on a Manchester council estate. His concept includes local accents, left‑hand driving and a range of “hustle” activities, showing how the game’s mechanics can be re‑skinned for a specific neighbourhood.

The article notes that after the commercial success and controversy of GTA III, many “GTA clones” emerged throughout the 2000s and 2010s, demonstrating that the core open‑world formula can be transplanted to diverse urban settings.
summary: Independent developers are creating Grand Theft Auto‑style open‑world games set in locations such as Manchester and Istanbul. They say Rockstar’s GTA III template can be placed in any city with enough people and cars, a practice that spawned many “GTA clones” after the original’s success.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meta launches UK AI shopping assistant Muse as retailers consider liability
content:
Meta is launching its Muse AI assistant in the UK this week, positioning it as a tool to find Black Friday deals, source Christmas gifts, and identify ingredients for romantic dinners. The company, which owns Facebook and Instagram, claims the launch will transform consumer shopping habits and retailer revenue streams.

While brands acknowledge that the use of such AI agents is increasing, they are unlikely to grant these tools full control over their sales processes. The rollout raises questions about liability, specifically asking who is responsible if the bot provides incorrect information or makes errors during the shopping experience.
summary: Meta launches UK AI shopping assistant Muse as retailers consider liability.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Natural England objects to Avonmouth AI datacentre weeks before ministers threaten agency
content:
Natural England formally objected to a proposed 40 MW artificial‑intelligence datacentre at Avonmouth, urging Bristol City Council to refuse planning permission. The agency cited the risk the development poses to protected wildlife and habitats, noting that the site lies within 600 metres of one of the United Kingdom’s most important locations for migratory birds.

The objection was lodged weeks before ministers announced a threat to abolish Natural England, the independent environmental adviser. The timing links the agency’s intervention on the datacentre with the broader governmental discussion about its future.
summary: Natural England objected to a 40MW AI datacentre at Avonmouth near Bristol, warning that the project threatens protected wildlife, habitats and a key migratory bird site within 600 metres. The objection was made weeks before ministers threatened to abolish the independent environmental adviser.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI agent completes first UK cardless purchase of Papa John’s pizzas
content:
An order of nine Papa John’s mini margherita pizzas has become the United Kingdom’s first purchase completed by an artificial‑intelligence agent using cardless payment technology. The transaction was carried out without the customer sharing bank security details and was conducted as part of a Financial Conduct Authority‑regulated sandbox trial. The trial involved Lloyds Bank and payment‑service provider TrueLayer.

The experiment highlights retailers’ growing interest in AI‑driven shopping assistants, a trend that is expected to expand as firms explore such technology ahead of high‑traffic periods like Black Friday.
summary: An AI agent made the first UK purchase using cardless payment technology when it ordered nine mini Papa John’s margherita pizzas. The transaction was part of the FCA’s sandbox trials and used Lloyds Bank and payment specialist TrueLayer, with no bank security details shared.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Labor leaders urge AI guardrails as Walmart's AI use harms workers
content: Labor leaders and consumer advocates are calling for safeguards as artificial‑intelligence tools become more common in U.S. retail operations. They say protections are needed for both workers and shoppers while AI use expands. On Black Friday, as millions of Americans begin holiday purchases, the impact of AI on the retail environment is already visible. Anna, a cashier at a Walmart in southern Oregon and a United for Respect leader who asked to stay anonymous over retaliation concerns, criticized Walmart’s AI implementation and its effects on employees.
summary: Labor leaders urge AI guardrails as Walmart's AI use harms workers.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meta whistleblower Sarah Wynn-Williams urges Andy Burnham to expand NDA ban
content:
Meta whistleblower Sarah Wynn‑Williams has urged Andy Burnham to strengthen the ban on non‑disclosure agreements. She says tech insiders who raise concerns about AI are being silenced in a system she compares to George Orwell’s 1984.

Wynn‑Williams, who served as the director of global public policy at Meta—then called Facebook—has been unable to discuss a series of allegations about the company’s treatment of teenagers that she details in her memoir because of restrictions imposed by the company. She warns that insiders concerned about AI development need protection.
summary: Sarah Wynn‑Williams, who served as director of global public policy at Meta (formerly Facebook), said tech insiders raising AI concerns are being silenced. She urged Andy Burnham to go further in banning non‑disclosure agreements, noting she cannot discuss allegations in her memoir because of company‑imposed restrictions.

title: Iran denies responsibility for Kuwait drone strike that killed two Italians

content: The EU summit on the Union’s common budget for 2028‑2034 collapsed early, according to the announcement. title: King tides and storms batter US coasts, damage pier in Pacifica, California
content:
Heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding have created hazardous conditions for millions traveling during the Thanksgiving period, as king tides and large waves have battered both U.S. coasts. The severe weather has prompted concerns about safety for holiday travelers across the country.

Along the California coast, the king tides caused notable damage in Pacifica, located south of San Francisco. On Wednesday, large waves struck the shoreline, destroying part of a pier and sending debris into the ocean. The National Weather Service responded by issuing coastal flood warnings for portions of the Pacific coastline as well as for shorelines around San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay.

In Pacifica, several beachfront properties have already experienced flooding. Additionally, authorities in Marin County temporarily issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront homes at Stinson Beach. The combined effects of the king tides and storm conditions have heightened risk for coastal communities during the holiday weekend.
summary: King tides and huge waves have battered both US coasts during the Thanksgiving period, creating hazardous conditions with heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding. In Pacifica, California, waves destroyed part of a pier, flooded beachfront properties and prompted National Weather Service flood warnings and a temporary evacuation warning for Stinson Beach homes.

content:

title: Disney+ Offers $4.99/Month Bundle for Full MCU Ahead of Avengers: Doomsday
content:
Avengers: Doomsday, set for release on December 18, is described as the biggest Marvel release of the year. To better understand the film’s storyline and multiverse details, viewers are encouraged to catch up on previous content available on Disney+. The platform hosts the entire Marvel Cinematic Universe catalog, which includes key television series such as Loki, VisionQuest, and Thunderbolts, alongside previous Avengers films. These titles are highlighted as essential viewing for anyone seeking a working understanding of the lore before the new movie arrives.

For those new to the multiverse concepts, the source recommends starting with the TV show Loki and the movie Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. These titles are said to break down the rules of the multiverse, exploring concepts such as timeline branching, superhero councils, and incursions. Additionally, the Fantastic Four reboot and the recently released VisionQuest are noted for introducing Dr. Doom, the titular villain of the upcoming release. The article advises paying attention to post-credits scenes for key character reveals and suggests that the original 2000s Fantastic Four films, featuring Chris Evans as the Human Torch, may also be of interest.

Specific recommendations are provided for different levels of familiarity with the franchise. For a general lore breakdown of the multiverse, viewers should watch Loki, Doctor Strange, and The Fantastic Four reboot. For direct preludes to the Avengers: Doomsday storyline, Thunderbolts and VisionQuest are identified as the key titles. Thunderbolts is noted to directly precede Doomsday by 14 months, while VisionQuest bridges the gap to the film, leading into its prelude.

Disney+ is also promoting a Black Friday bundle deal that includes access to both Disney+ and Hulu for $4.99 per month for 12 months. This ad-supported bundle represents a 62% discount from the usual $12.99 price point. The subscription provides access to nearly every Marvel movie and series, as well as extensive non-Marvel libraries including Star Wars, Pixar, National Geographic, and Alien. Hulu content included in the bundle features shows such as Shōgun, The Bear, Paradise, and X-Files.

The premium version of the bundle is also discounted, dropping from $21.99 to $14.99 per month. The source states that the standard bundle saves subscribers $96 over the year, while the premium bundle saves $84. This offer is intended for new and lapsed subscriptions, as it is not applicable to existing Disney+ subscribers. For viewers less interested in Marvel, the bundle offers other sci-fi options like Alien: Earth and The Testaments, along with the entire Star Wars franchise.
summary: Disney+ Offers $4.99/Month Bundle for Full MCU Ahead of Avengers: Doomsday.

title: Dark Energy Camera captures striking blue Betta Fish Nebula in Centaurus
content:
The Betta Fish Nebula, a supernova remnant located approximately 6,800 light-years from Earth in the Centaurus constellation, has been featured in a new cosmic portrait. Formed by the explosion of a star significantly more massive than the sun, the nebula is a wisp of gas and dust that has expanded and collided with surrounding interstellar medium over time. This interaction has resulted in a glowing, blue cloud that resembles a fish, earning it its distinctive nickname.

The image was captured by the Dark Energy Camera (DECam), an instrument created by the U.S. Department of Energy. DECam is installed on the National Science Foundation’s Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile. While the camera is primarily designed to study the effects of dark energy, the mysterious force causing the universe’s expansion to accelerate, it is also capable of producing striking astronomical imagery.

DECam serves as a key tool for the Dark Energy Survey, a six-year international collaboration that has gathered observations of hundreds of millions of galaxies and thousands of supernovae. Although initial results from this survey were revealed in January, scientists continue to use DECam to explore the nature of dark energy. These ongoing efforts are conducted alongside other instruments, including the recently launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, to further understand the cosmos.
summary: The Betta Fish Nebula is a supernova remnant located roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth in the Centaurus constellation. This image was captured by the Dark Energy Camera installed on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile.
author: Space.com

title: London Broncos target new venues and Australia‑friendly times after Super League return
content:
London Broncos are targeting new venues and Australia-friendly kick-off times, including Thursday and Saturday lunchtime slots, following their return to the Super League. The Rugby Football League awarded the club the 15th spot in the newly expanded competition for 2027. Last year, the Broncos dominated the Championship, losing only one league fixture and securing a domestic treble with a squad widely considered ready for the top flight.

title: Steelers owner backs McCarthy, calls Rodgers' actions insubordination
content:
Pittsburgh Steelers owner and president Art Rooney II has expressed “100% confidence” in head coach Mike McCarthy following a public dispute with quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Rooney II characterized Rodgers’s recent actions as “insubordination” and stated that such outbursts could not be tolerated. The comments come after Rodgers was benched on Tuesday night and subsequently waived by the team.

The conflict escalated after Rodgers appeared on The Pat McAfee Show, where he accused McCarthy of falling asleep during a meeting. Rodgers further alleged that the head coach missed meetings and a walkthrough later that same week. These claims were corroborated by unnamed sources in a Wednesday report by ESPN.

With Rodgers no longer on the roster, the Steelers are preparing to face the Denver Broncos on Friday. Mason Rudolph is set to start at quarterback for the upcoming game.
summary: Art Rooney II expressed full confidence in head coach Mike McCarthy and labeled Aaron Rodgers' recent outbursts as intolerable insubordination. Rodgers was benched and waived after accusing McCarthy of falling asleep during a meeting, with the Steelers preparing to face Denver with Mason Rudolph at quarterback.

content:

content:

title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
content:

The match had seen Palace trailing to a Mamadou Sarr goal, but the game swung in their favour 17 minutes from full‑time when Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean‑Philippe Mateta an equaliser.

The French striker capitalised on the dismissal, converting a penalty to level the score. Dwight McNeil then finished the comeback, scoring after an own goal in Saturday’s loss to Coventry. The win came in Frank’s first home match since taking over from Pierre Sage.

Despite a Yéremy Pino penalty saved in stoppage time and several missed chances, Dean Henderson made a decisive late save to seal the result, reviving Palace’s Europa League hopes. The club now heads into Sunday’s crucial encounter with Hull with renewed confidence.
