title: Avi Davidson uses first home‑tested bionic LUKE arm that provides tactile feedback
content:
Avi Davidson, a 33‑year‑old trauma therapist who lost his left hand at age 16, is the ninth participant to receive an experimental bionic LUKE arm and the first to use the device at home. The prosthetic, named after a fictional character, was originally developed in the 2000s, first trialed in 2014 and cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration that same year. Davidson’s involvement centers on a new method of linking the arm to the nerves in his residual forearm, allowing both motor control and pressure feedback.

Davidson’s injury occurred in 2009 when he fell from a telephone pole, suffered extensive burns, broken ribs, a severed spinal cord and gangrene that led to amputation of his dominant left hand. After a month in a coma, he underwent rehabilitation and has since used a series of prosthetic devices, ranging from a basic hook to more advanced models that respond to muscle movements. In a chance meeting with a scientist, he was recruited for the University of Utah’s neurorobotics trial, which required extensive physical and psychological screening, brain imaging to confirm a mental representation of his left hand, and nerve function testing.

Surgery in late January placed three electrode arrays—each with 100 needles—into three forearm nerves, and 24 additional electrodes into surrounding muscles. The arrays were inserted with a compressed‑air device and left protruding from the skin for connection to external hardware. After a brief recovery, Davidson began training a computer system to translate his nerve signals into hand, wrist and finger movements, a process that took minutes for motor mapping but required three days of stimulation testing to establish sensory feedback.

Once the wiring was simplified to a plug‑like connection, Davidson could attach the prosthetic, power it with a small computer and begin daily use. Occupational therapist Leanne Seckinger worked with him on functional tasks such as cooking, and Davidson reports rapid improvement—from taking minutes to write his name to completing the task in seconds. He now wears the hand six days a week, recharging batteries twice daily, and notes occasional phantom‑pain sensations and wrist strain that he can relieve by pulling the bionic fingers back.

The trial aims to assess how the two‑way interface performs in everyday life, its benefits, limitations and effects on users’ well‑being, brain and nervous system. Researchers hope the data will support broader FDA approval and insurance coverage, and eventually enable control of other devices such as wheelchairs. The study is slated to run for at least one year, ending in January 2027, with the possibility of extension pending funding. Davidson acknowledges that he will not keep the device after the trial, but remains motivated by the prospect of advancing the technology for future patients.
summary: Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: UK FCA says Meta declined to share Muse for joint testing ahead of agent rollout
content: Meta declined a request to share its Muse platform for joint testing, prompting a complaint from the UK Financial Conduct Authority. The FCA warned that the refusal could represent “another force of attack” from agents, noting the issue arose ahead of Meta’s scheduled rollout of its personal agent in the UK on Tuesday.
summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority warned of “another force of attack” from agents after Meta refused a request to share its Muse tool for joint testing. The refusal came ahead of the rollout of Meta’s personal agent in the UK on Tuesday.
author: Wired

title: Gemini AI enhances Android Auto with navigation and idea brainstorming
content: Android Auto now incorporates Gemini, a new AI feature that makes the system smarter. According to the announcement, Gemini helps users navigate more easily and lets them bounce ideas off the AI while driving.
summary: Android Auto now includes Gemini AI, making the system smarter. The Gemini integration allows easier navigation and lets users bounce ideas while driving.
author: Wired

title: 42 state AGs seek to block Character.AI sale of user chat data
content:
A coalition of 42 state attorneys general has filed a coordinated effort to block Character.AI from selling user data while the company proceeds through Chapter 11 bankruptcy. The attorneys general allege that Character.AI intends to auction the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including over 2.1 million accounts registered to minors, without any safeguards for the individuals whose conversations would be sold.

Character.AI entered bankruptcy in October after a series of scandals and legal challenges, one of which involved Disney. Disney subsequently purchased certain assets of the company and hired its chief executive officer. The attorneys general’s press releases, which are largely identical, focus on preventing the proposed data sale.
summary: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character. AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings.
author: The Verge

title: X launches first parental controls for teen accounts
content:
X is rolling out parental controls that let parents and guardians manage teens' accounts on the platform. Teens retain ownership of their own account.

Parents can see how much time their child has spent on X, set daily limits, require approval for new followers, and limit For You recommendations to accounts a teen already follows. Parents cannot read private messages, see searches or viewing history, post as their teen, or access the account. Every change is recorded and visible to the teen.
summary: X launches first parental controls for teen accounts.
author: The Verge

title: Waymo robotaxi attempts to overtake CHP cruisers on I‑280, prompting DMV interstate ban
content:
On November 6, a driverless Waymo robotaxi on Interstate 280 attempted to overtake two California Highway Patrol cruisers during a traffic‑break maneuver, an action that constitutes a moving violation that could lead to a human driver’s license suspension. The incident was captured on video and added to a series of freeway errors that prompted the California Department of Motor Vehicles, last week, to ban Waymo vehicles from all state interstates.

Waymo has also reported difficulties in construction zones; between October and November 2026 the company logged a total of 11 such instances. These challenges contrast with the company’s success operating robotaxis on city streets.
summary: On November 6, a driverless Waymo robotaxi tried to overtake two California Highway Patrol cruisers during a traffic break on Interstate 280, a moving violation. The incident was among several freeway errors that led the California DMV last week to ban Waymo vehicles from all state interstates.
author: The Verge

title: Ars Technica staff showcase diverse home office setups from minimalist to maximalist
content: Ars Technica is a place that has always leaned into remote working. Since its beginnings in 1998, Ars has never had a single, central office—a setup that makes for a great commute to work, with little risk of getting stuck in traffic. As Ars staffers step away from their desks for a few days to spend some time with family and friends, we wanted to give you a look inside our home offices. We've got all sorts of setups, tucked into basements, dens, spare bedrooms, apartment corners, and lofts. They run the gamut from minimalist "here's my laptop and monitor" setups to "I really like collecting things." Without any further ado, let's dig in: Jeremy Hsu Living in a New York apartment means being smart with available space. Credit: Jeremy Hsu/Ars Technica As an apartment dweller in New York City, I’ve usually set up my home work station in a small corner of my residence along with sometimes decamping for local cafes or coworking spaces. My current hodgepodge of equipment is probably on the minimal side compared to many members of the Ars team. Read full article Comments
summary: Ars Technica has operated without a central office since its founding in 1998, relying on remote work. The article displays staff home office spaces—from basements and lofts to a New York apartment corner—showing setups that range from minimalist laptop‑only stations to more elaborate collections.
author: Ars Technica

title: Investigators probe Nvidia's knowledge of chip destinations and Huang's Megaspeed ties
content: Investigators are focusing on two key issues: what Nvidia knew about the ultimate destination of certain chips, and whether Jensen Huang’s personal relationship with a Megaspeed executive provided the company with reason to question Megaspeed’s assurances. These questions remain unanswered.
summary: Investigators are questioning what Nvidia knew about where the chips ended up. They are also examining whether Jensen Huang's affair with a Megaspeed executive gave the company reason to doubt Megaspeed's assurances.
author: TechCrunch

title: Mount Kalaga in GTA VI offers bike and hiking trails and eagle spotting
content:
The source highlights Mount Kalaga as a destination for players who want a break from the crime and violence in GTA VI. It notes that the mountain offers both bike trails and hiking trails that ascend to its summit.

In addition to the trails, the area provides hunting opportunities and birdwatching; the author mentions choosing birdwatching over deer hunting and reports spotting an eagle on the mountain.
summary: The piece highlights Mount Kalaga as a getaway spot in GTA VI. The mountain provides bike and hiking trails, hunting options and birdwatching, where an eagle was observed.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI misuse impacts over 25 England and Wales court cases in 2026
content:
An investigation has identified at least 25 court cases in England and Wales in 2026 that were affected by undisclosed use of artificial intelligence. Judges reported encountering AI‑generated witness statements, fictitious case law and references to nonexistent statutes, prompting formal complaints about the misuse.

Among the affected proceedings was a High Court dispute between tax lawyers, which a judge described as involving “unacceptable” use of “generative AI hallucinations” and citations to cases that do not exist. The findings highlight the extent of AI misuse by lawyers, police officers and claimants in the current year.
summary: An investigation found that undisclosed AI use affected at least 25 court cases in England and Wales in 2026, involving AI‑generated witness statements, fictitious case law and nonexistent statutes. Judges complained about the misuse, including a high‑court tax‑law dispute where a judge described the generative‑AI hallucinations and references to nonexistent cases as unacceptable.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Elon Musk pledges two SpaceX shares for every US child, valued at nearly $18 bn
content:
Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, announced on his social‑media platform X that he will give every child in the United States two shares in SpaceX, the space and AI company he runs. According to the post, the combined value of the shares could total almost $18 billion, with one share coming directly from SpaceX and the other from Musk personally.

In a related statement released earlier on Wednesday, SpaceX said it will issue one newly created Class A common‑stock share to every currently active Trump Account. Musk added that he will match the number of shares the company donates, effectively providing a second share for each child. The pledge and the company’s contribution were presented together as part of the same initiative.
summary: Elon Musk pledges two SpaceX shares for every US child, valued at nearly $18 bn.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Tech leaders cheer Jensen Huang's Nvidia CEO return, Google, Meta, Apple silent
content:
A vocal subsection of the tech industry marked Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s chief executive on Monday, with the phrase “return of the king” trending on social media. Posts ranged from calling him “imperial and royal majesty” and “our Jesus” to adding crown emojis. Elon Musk said, “The mistake has been corrected,” and OpenAI founder Sam Altman exclaimed, “Jensen!”

In contrast, the heads of Google, Meta and Apple have not offered any comment on Huang’s reinstatement.
summary: Tech leaders cheer Jensen Huang's Nvidia CEO return, Google, Meta, Apple silent.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Trump thanks Uzbekistan for walnut‑wood pavilions gifted to Washington park
content: President Trump thanked Uzbekistan for gifting traditional pavilions to a Washington park. The structures, crafted from wood of 200‑year‑old walnut trees, are situated near several of the city’s well‑known monuments and commemorate the independence anniversaries of both nations.
summary: The pavilions were crafted from the wood of 200‑year‑old walnut trees and stand near Washington’s best‑known monuments. The gift commemorates the independence anniversaries of both countries.
author: Euronews

title: Explosion at Bangchak oil facility in eastern Bangkok sends black smoke over city
content: A major explosion erupted at a Bangchak oil facility in eastern Bangkok on Thursday, sending flames and thick black smoke over the city. Authorities instructed nearby residents to evacuate while emergency services responded to the incident.
summary: A major explosion occurred at a Bangchak oil facility in eastern Bangkok on Thursday, sending flames and thick black smoke into the sky. Authorities urged nearby residents to evacuate while emergency services responded to the incident.
author: Euronews

title: Fuel tanker crash on Giza Ring Road kills 31, injures 21
content: A fuel tanker crash on Giza’s Ring Road in Waraq sparked a massive fire that left at least 31 people dead and 21 injured. The incident, which produced wreckage and burnt vehicles, underscores the hazardous nature of Egypt’s road conditions.
summary: A massive fire from a fuel tanker crash on Giza’s Ring Road in Waraq killed at least 31 people. The incident also injured 21 others and highlighted Egypt’s deadly road risks.
author: Euronews

title: UK sent convicted Sri Lankan refugee to Eswatini in secret deal, BBC reports
content: The BBC investigation reports that the United Kingdom sent a Sri Lankan refugee, who had been convicted of sexual assault, to Eswatini. In Eswatini, the refugee committed suicide. The transfer was part of a secret deal, according to the BBC.
summary: The United Kingdom reportedly sent a Sri Lankan refugee who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini. He later committed suicide, and a BBC investigation described the transfer as part of a secret deal.
author: Euronews

title: Kim Jong Un inspects nuclear facilities and urges arsenal expansion
content: Images released show North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspecting nuclear material production facilities and a weapons‑research institute. Following the visits, Kim called for expanding the country’s nuclear arsenal.
summary: Kim Jong Un visited nuclear material production facilities and a weapons research institute. He called for expanding North Korea's nuclear arsenal.
author: Euronews

title: Trump unveils new tariffs on 14 trade partners over 'unfair' industrial capacity
content:
US President Donald Trump announced a new tariff package on Wednesday targeting 14 major trading partners, including China, Japan and the European Union. The administration’s move comes as Trump continues his protectionist agenda, despite the Republican Party’s losses in the recent U.S. midterm elections.

The proposed tariffs would set maximum potential rates ranging from 20 % to 40 %. They are intended to counter what the administration claims is excess industrial capacity promoted by the targeted countries.
summary: Trump unveils new tariffs on 14 trade partners over 'unfair' industrial capacity.
author: France 24

title: France pushes to safeguard CAP subsidies in EU budget talks
content:
Leaders from EU countries are meeting in Brussels on Thursday and Friday for another round of talks on the EU's next multi‑year budget.

For France, the main aim of the negotiations is to prevent a reduction in the funding allocated to the Common Agricultural Policy, a subsidy vital for French agriculture – a position Macron made clear in a meeting with farmers unions in Paris on Wednesday.
summary: Leaders from EU countries are meeting in Brussels on Thursday and Friday for another round of talks on the EU's next multi‑year budget. France aims to prevent any reduction in funding for the Common Agricultural Policy, a stance Macron reiterated in a meeting with farmers unions in Paris on Wednesday.
author: France 24

title: French Prefect Hugues Moutouh Removed Over Suspected National Rally Leak
content:
Two senior French officials are now subject to investigations over alleged leaks to the far‑right National Rally. The prefect of Loiret, identified as former Interior Ministry senior official Hugues Moutouh, has been removed from his post after suspicion that he passed confidential information concerning investigations to the party.

A Paris deputy prosecutor, discovered at the National Rally headquarters during a police search, is also facing an administrative inquiry related to the same suspected leaks.
summary: The prefect of the Loiret, Hugues Moutouh, was removed from his post after being suspected of passing confidential information about investigations to the National Rally. A deputy prosecutor in Paris, found at the party's headquarters during a police search, is now under administrative inquiry.
author: France 24

title: Mediapart and Le Monde Publish New Messages Alleging Jordan Bardella's Anti‑Semitic Views
content:
French media outlets Mediapart and Le Monde have released an additional collection of messages that they say demonstrate far‑right leader Jordan Bardella’s “rampant anti‑Semitic thoughts” from his time as a young party member in 2013.  

In other news, France is conducting the first trial of a female jihadist, Émilie König, while Kilmar Abrego Garcia—identified in the review as once the face of Donald Trump’s “brutal mass deportations”—has arrived in Spain. A separate piece examines why the rich world is experiencing a “sex recession.”
summary: Mediapart and Le Monde released a trove of messages that allegedly show far‑right leader Jordan Bardella's anti‑Semitic thoughts from 2013. The documents suggest he expressed these thoughts while a young party member.
author: France 24

title: Emily Konig on trial in Paris for alleged IS propaganda
content:
Emily Konig, accused of being one of the Islamic State’s most active French propagandists, went on trial in Paris on Thursday. She faces a charge of criminal association with a terrorist organisation and could receive up to 30 years in prison if convicted.  

Originally from Brittany, Konig spent a decade in Syria before returning to France in 2022. France 24’s Luke Shrago is following the proceedings in Paris and has joined the coverage to explain the defence’s strategy.
summary: Accused of being one of the Islamic State group's most active French propagandists, Emily Konig went on trial in Paris on Thursday. Originally from Brittany, Konig spent a decade in Syria before returning to France in 2022.
author: France 24

title: 31 killed in Cairo after fuel truck overturns, driver arrested
content: A fire erupted on a busy Cairo highway on Wednesday after a fuel truck overturned, killing at least 31 people. The suspected driver was arrested the following day, according to Egypt’s public prosecutor’s office.
summary: A fire broke out on a busy highway in Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people after a fuel truck reportedly overturned. The suspected driver was arrested on Thursday, according to Egypt’s public prosecutor’s office.
author: France 24

title: French far-right leader Bardella faces fresh anti-Semitism accusations in media reports
content:
On Thursday, French media reported fresh accusations against National Rally president Jordan Bardella, alleging antisemitic remarks made in 2013 chats during his teenage years.

These claims build on earlier allegations published by investigative outlet Mediapart in September, which said Bardella had made a slew of antisemitic and conspiratorial comments.

Bardella denies making antisemitic remarks. France 24’s French Politics Editor Marc Perelman will provide additional context.
summary: French far-right leader Bardella faces fresh anti-Semitism accusations in media reports.
author: France 24

title: European Council President Antonio Costa urges leaders to compromise on EU budget by year‑end
content: European Council President Antonio Costa urged European leaders to seek compromise on the bloc's long-term budget at a summit Thursday, as Brussels pushes to lock in the plans before next year's French election where far-right leader Marine Le Pen is leading in opinion polls. "Now it is time for all of the leaders to participate in this debate with an open mind, a constructive approach, and a sense of compromise. Because we need to approve this budget timely. That means by the end of this year," Costa said. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels, Belgium.
summary: European Council President Antonio Costa urged European leaders to seek compromise on the EU’s long‑term budget at a Thursday summit, saying it must be approved by the end of the year. Brussels wants to lock in the budget before next year’s French election, where far‑right leader Marine Le Pen is leading in opinion polls.
author: France 24

title: Russia develops Rassvet satellite system as potential counter to Starlink in Ukraine
content: SpaceX’s Starlink satellite system has been described as having played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine. A Russian counterpart to Starlink, known as Rassvet, is currently under development, prompting speculation about how it could affect Ukraine’s situation in the future.
summary: SpaceX's Starlink has played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine. Russia is developing a counterpart called Rassvet, which could affect Ukraine's future communications.

title: Chinese firms use Southeast Asian offshore computing to bypass US AI chip restrictions
content: High‑tech AI chips are difficult for Chinese firms to obtain because of U.S. restrictions. To bypass these limits, Chinese companies frequently rely on offshore computing capacity, especially in Southeast Asia. The United States is actively working to halt this circumvention.
summary: US restrictions make high‑tech AI chips difficult to obtain in China. Chinese companies therefore use offshore computing capacity in Southeast Asia to bypass the sanctions, while the United States seeks to stop the practice.
author: DW World

title: Kyiv attacks Russian vessels worldwide to pressure Moscow, signal allies
content: Kyiv’s attacks on Russian vessels are occurring worldwide, including the Baltic and the Mediterranean, as part of an effort to increase pressure on Moscow and to send signals to its Western allies. The article raises the question of how these actions are affecting global maritime trade.
summary: Kyiv is attacking Russian vessels around the world. The attacks aim to increase pressure on Moscow and send signals to its Western allies.
author: DW World

title: One crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza, 17 rescued
content: A diesel tanker sank off the coast of Ibiza, prompting authorities to rescue 17 crew members. One of those rescued later died in hospital. In response, a contingency plan to address possible pollution damage has been implemented.
summary: Authorities rescued 17 crew members after a diesel tanker sank off the Spanish island of Ibiza, but one crew member later died in hospital. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage has been put in place.
author: DW World

title: Norse Atlantic Airways suspends all flights, threatens bankruptcy without funding
content:
Norse Atlantic Airways announced on Thursday that it has suspended all flights and will file for bankruptcy if it cannot obtain urgent short‑term financing. The airline described its financial situation as “critical” and said the funding shortfall leaves it on the brink of collapse.

The carrier, which operates long‑haul routes worldwide—including services from London Gatwick and between the United States, Europe and Asia—issued the suspension a day after previously warning that its finances were critical. It indicated that securing immediate backing is essential to avoid bankruptcy proceedings.
summary: Norse Atlantic Airways suspends all flights, threatens bankruptcy without funding.
author: Guardian World

title: MPs say ministers failed to justify Heathrow third runway, citing economic and climate shortfalls
content: The Commons transport committee released a report on Thursday stating that ministers have “failed to make the case” for a third runway at Heathrow. The committee’s assessment draws on detailed government policy papers, which it says demonstrate that expanding the London airport would not meet the government’s pledges on the economy and on climate. The MPs’ report characterises the evidence as falling short of the commitments set out for economic and environmental objectives.
summary: The Commons transport committee said ministers have “failed to make the case” for a third runway at Heathrow. It added that the government’s policy papers show expanding the London airport would fall short of pledges on the economy and climate.
author: Guardian World

title: EU leaders far apart on budget agreement, says Giorgia Meloni
content: A number of leaders hope to agree to a budget before consequential elections around the continent The Danish prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, has acknowledged that leaders remain “very far apart,” agreeing with Germany’s Merz that the current proposal is not going to work. “The budget is too large and not sufficiently future-oriented,” she said, calling for more work on competitiveness, defence and security.
summary: EU leaders far apart on budget agreement, says Giorgia Meloni.

title: Coalition to privatise Melbourne sewage plants and sell state land and renewables if it wins election
content:
The Liberal and Nationals’ pre‑election policy costings, released by opposition leader Jess Wilson on Thursday, outline a plan for a Victorian Coalition government. If elected, the coalition would privatise two sewage plants and sell state‑owned land, renewable energy assets, and the “air rights” between Richmond train station and the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

Wilson issued the costings just two days before the state election, after more than 1.5 million Victorians had already cast their ballots. The documents present the parties’ key promises and policy details ahead of the vote.
summary: Coalition to privatise Melbourne sewage plants and sell state land and renewables if it wins election.
author: Guardian World

title: Labor inquiry says new defence laws could have significant human rights impact
content:
A Labor‑chaired inquiry warned that new defence legislation granting officials the authority to use lethal force against suspected trespassers in designated zones could have “significant” human‑rights implications. The committee highlighted the absence of requirements to provide detained individuals with fresh drinking water or humane conditions, and cautioned that the broad changes might affect members of the public who inadvertently enter a defence security zone that has not been publicised.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese defended the laws, describing criticism of them as “nonsense” and “conspiracy theories” from the far left and far right.
summary: Labor inquiry says new defence laws could have significant human rights impact.
author: Guardian World

title: Senate inquiry says Labor's Support at Home program leaves older Australians without care
content: The Support at Home system has ‘baffling’ bureaucracy and ‘rations and denies care’, says Greens chair of Senate inquiry Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast Many older Australians are dying before they can access home support, paying exorbitant fees, and being pushed into hospitals and residential care before they are ready because of a flawed federal government aged care program, a Senate inquiry has found. The inquiry is examining the impact of the Support at Home program, which launched in November 2025 and has been plagued by complaints of making care harder to access and more expensive. The inquiry was due to finish in November, but has been extended for a further year after receiving almost 300 submissions.
summary: The Senate inquiry found that the federal Support at Home program, launched in November 2025, is plagued by “baffling” bureaucracy, high fees and delays that leave many older Australians dying before receiving care. The inquiry, chaired by the Greens senator, has been extended for a year after receiving almost 300 submissions.
author: Guardian World

title: Wife of Japanese journalist Yuki Imai pleads for his release after Russia detains him
content:
The wife of Japanese journalist Yuki Imai has issued an emotional appeal for his release after he has been detained in Russia for more than a month on suspicion of spying. Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid‑October while preparing to return to Japan from a two‑year assignment at the newspaper’s bureau in Yuzhno‑Sakhalinsk on Sakhalin Island.

Imai is being held in Moscow on allegations that he conducted “espionage” while working for the newspaper in Russia’s far east. The wife’s plea highlights her distress and her request that the authorities reconsider his detention.
summary: Yuki Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid‑October in Moscow on suspicion of espionage while preparing to return to Japan from a two‑year assignment in Yuzhno‑Sakhalinsk, Sakhalin. His wife has issued an emotional appeal asking for his release after more than a month of detention.
author: Guardian World

title: China says it may take necessary measures after Trump proposes 20% tariff
content: Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’, while Brazil ‘will not yield to this type of threat’ Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU Beijing has said it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” after Donald Trump’s administration proposed new tariffs on goods from China and other major trading partners, triggering a global backlash. Among the suggested levies on 14 major trading partners announced on Wednesday, China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. It would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.
summary: China says it may take necessary measures after Trump proposes 20% tariff.
author: Guardian World

title: Bob Woodward's memoir 'Secrets' details his career and the craft of investigative reporting
content: The journalist who helped bring down Nixon on false starts, Watergate, and the art of cultivating a source ‘I have always disliked the term ‘investigative reporter’.” So writes Bob Woodward, one of the most celebrated reporters of our time – the man whose Watergate reporting with Carl Bernstein undoubtedly changed the US presidency and journalism itself for ever. His longtime boss, the Washington Post editor Ben Bradlee, disliked the term too: “All reporting is investigative,” Bradlee would say. The term conjures a certain sophistication, perhaps, but part of the beauty of a reporter’s work is how deceptively unsophisticated it can be. Secrets is a far-ranging, revealing memoir of an extraordinary career, but more than that, it is an ode to grinding it out – knocking on doors, asking and asking again, listening, taking notes, making notes on the notes, patiently following every lead to exhaustion. In a media ecosystem saturated with fast and flimsy takes, this feels like a tonic. The real star of his story, Woodward seems to insist, is the shoe leather.
summary: Bob Woodward's memoir 'Secrets' is a far-ranging account of his extraordinary career, including his Watergate reporting with Carl Bernstein. The book emphasizes the deceptively unsophisticated nature of reporting, focusing on persistence and following leads.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Review: Jon Fosse's Vaim Hotel sequel explores surreal captivity in new novel
content:
Jon Fosse’s 2025 novel, Vaim Hotel, serves as the second volume in a loosely connected trilogy set in the fictional Norwegian town of Vaim. The book is a sequel to Vaim and explores the experience of a man who is stripped of the elements that define his identity. Translated by Damion Searls, the narrative is written in Fosse’s characteristic hypnotically recursive style, consisting of a single sentence.

The story begins with a man in his 50s who drives to Vaim for reasons he cannot fully articulate. He decides to stay at the empty Vaim Hotel, unaware that he may never leave. The novel features Brita, the hotel owner, a mysterious female figure before whom the male protagonist’s agency fails. This dynamic mirrors the themes of the predecessor, where a man encounters a woman he secretly loved in his youth. In that earlier volume, the woman requests to move with him to their hometown on a boat named after her, despite being married.

The predecessor, Vaim, also depicts a man who has died, with the woman returning to her husband and demanding he answer to a specific name and move into the home of the man she had previously left him for. The husband describes these events as strange and chooses that word for his tombstone. Reviewers note that both books feature a sense of powerlessness in the men and a dream-like, surreal randomness to the events.

Fosse’s narrative choices in Vaim Hotel are described as thwarting easy rationalization. The work is characterized as Beckettian in its appreciation for the absurd and the tediously mundane. It is presented as a tale of captivity that is only slightly less disorienting than its predecessor, owing to the thematic connections between the two volumes.
summary: Jon Fosse's new novel Vaim Hotel is the second volume in a trilogy set in the fictional Norwegian town of Vaim. The book features a man who lodges at the empty Vaim Hotel under the influence of its owner, Brita, in a story described as a tale of captivity.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Photographer Niall McDiarmid captures vibrant colors to counter muted world
content: Photographer Niall McDiarmid seeks out vivid colours, such as bright green kebab shops and red stockings, to counteract what he describes as a muted beige and monochrome world. The accompanying visual feature highlights these vibrant scenes as antidotes to everyday dullness.
summary: Photographer Niall McDiarmid seeks out bright colors, such as green kebab shops and red stockings, to provide an antidote to the world's muted beige and monochrome tones.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran guitarist, dies at 65
content:
Andy Taylor, the guitarist for the 1980s pop band Duran Duran, has died at the age of 65.

He was diagnosed with stage four metastatic prostate cancer in 2018, and publicly disclosed the diagnosis in 2022 as the band approached induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

Taylor’s career was marked by significant chart success during the 1980s.
summary: Andy Taylor, the guitarist for 1980s pop band Duran Duran, died at age 65. He had been diagnosed with stage four metastatic prostate cancer in 2018 and publicly disclosed the diagnosis in 2022 as the band approached their Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Strabane withdraws UK Town of Culture 2028 bid after causing division
content: The County Tyrone town was shortlisted as one of 15 possible locations for the inaugural UK Town of Culture 2028, with the chance to win £3m.
summary: Strabane, a town in County Tyrone, was shortlisted as one of 15 possible locations for the inaugural UK Town of Culture 2028, with a chance to win £3 million. The bid was later withdrawn after it caused great division.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Aaron Rodgers accuses Steelers coach Mike McCarthy of misconduct in ESPN interview
content: From a half-time huddle gone wrong to an ultimatum over play-calling, here’s what the quarterback said Wednesday in a scorched-earth appearance on Pat McAfee’s show Barely 12 hours after the Pittsburgh Steelers announced that Aaron Rodgers would be deactivated and Mason Rudolph would start Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos, the four-time NFL Most Valuable Player left no bridge unburned in a surprise call-in to ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show. In a 34-minute appearance on Wednesday afternoon where he spoke uninterrupted for long stretches, Rodgers accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep in a quarterback meeting, skipping walkthroughs and falling behind on film study. He also said the 63-year-old McCarthy broke a half-time huddle against Philadelphia with the words “One, two, three, Packers”. According to Rodgers, McCarthy denied falling asleep at the team facility.
summary: Aaron Rodgers appeared on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show to criticize Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy's preparation and play-calling. Rodgers alleged that McCarthy fell asleep in a meeting and used incorrect team names during a half-time huddle.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alejandro Garnacho left out of Aston Villa plans despite Unai Emery's interest
content:
Unai Emery has reportedly left out Alejandro Garnacho from Aston Villa’s plans, a decision that mirrors the treatment of Harvey Elliott last season despite the club’s ongoing attacking struggles. This week marks three years since Garnacho scored for Manchester United in a 3-3 Champions League draw against Galatasaray in Istanbul. At that time, the winger was a teenage star and a regular starter, having recently won the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award for an overhead kick at Goodison Park.

During that period, Garnacho was central to Manchester United’s future, sharing the pitch with Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, who are now his teammates at Aston Villa. He continued to perform well, scoring twice in a 3-2 victory against Villa on Boxing Day and again in a win over West Ham, which led to a memorable celebration with Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund. Garnacho concluded that season by scoring against Manchester City at Wembley in the FA Cup final, cementing his status as a beacon of hope for the club alongside Mainoo.
summary: Unai Emery wanted the winger, but Alejandro Garnacho has been left out in the cold at Aston Villa despite the club's attacking struggles. The article notes this situation is similar to Harvey Elliott's experience at the club last season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Gukesh and Sindarov draw Game 2 of world chess championship in 20 moves
content:
India’s Gukesh Dommaraju and Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov drew the second game of their world chess championship match on Wednesday at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in the Geneva suburbs. The encounter concluded in just 20 moves and 1 hour 57 minutes, ending by threefold repetition. This result leaves the overall match score level at 1–all.

The game was notably brief, marking one of the shortest classical world title games since the reunification of rival championships in 2006. It was also the first game to finish in under two hours since Ding Liren and Ian Nepomniachtchi drew their 11th game in just over 100 minutes in Astana in 2023.

In this encounter, World champion Gukesh opened with the London System. The next game is scheduled for Thursday, with Sindarov set to play with the white pieces.
summary: India’s Gukesh Dommaraju and Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov drew the second game of their world chess championship match in 20 moves, leaving the score level at 1-all. Sindarov will play with white in Game 3 on Thursday at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in the Geneva suburbs.
author: Guardian Sport

content: Liverpool defeated Club Brugge in a clinical Champions League match, bouncing back from a previous defeat. Alexander Isak scored twice, with Florian Wirtz also finding the net to secure the victory for the hosts.
summary: Liverpool defeated Club Brugge in a clinical performance to bounce back from a previous Champions League defeat. Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz scored goals for the winning team.

title: Isak scores twice against Club Brugge to reach 10 goals for Liverpool
content: Alexander Isak scored two goals against Club Brugge, increasing his season tally to ten. The striker continues to demonstrate the value of Liverpool’s £125m transfer fee from last year.
summary: Alexander Isak scored two goals against Club Brugge, bringing his season total to 10. His performance continues to demonstrate the value of Liverpool's £125m transfer fee for the striker.

But he’s definitely a grandmaster of politics,” Kushner said…

content: A Fulton County, Ga., judge on Wednesday paused her own order requiring the county to provide copies of ballots seized by the FBI earlier this year to the Georgia State Election Board. Superior Court Judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe suspended the directive, which she had issued Tuesday, after county election officials filed a notice of appeal.
summary: A Fulton County judge paused her order for the county to turn over seized 2020 ballot copies to the Georgia State Election Board. The judge acted after county election officials filed a notice of appeal regarding the order issued Tuesday.

title: Mayor Mamdani to miss postponed Macy's Thanksgiving parade due to Achilles surgery
content: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) will miss the postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving parade on Saturday due to scheduled surgery on his right leg. The mayor confirmed at a Wednesday press conference that he is undergoing the procedure on Friday after tearing his Achilles tendon. Mamdani stated he was “very disappointed” to be unable to attend the rescheduled event.
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani will miss the postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving parade because he is scheduled to have right‑leg Achilles tendon surgery on Friday. He confirmed at a Wednesday press conference that he could not attend the rescheduled event and expressed disappointment.

content: Federal officials lifted a shelter-in-place order in Middletown, Iowa, on Wednesday following a controlled detonation of unstable explosive material at the Iowa Ammunition Plant. content: U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan, a Biden-era appointee, granted a preliminary injunction Wednesday night blocking the Federal Communications Commission from proceeding with the early renewal of ABC’s broadcast licenses. title: Rod Simms argues Australia should tax gas industry to boost revenue
content:
Rod Simms argues that increasing tax revenue from Australia’s gas industry is a straightforward public policy measure. He notes that fossil fuel companies currently do not pay for the natural resources their businesses rely on. Simms contends that while there are calls for the government to return the budget to surplus, achieving this through large expenditure cuts is difficult due to rising costs associated with an ageing population and defence spending.

Simms suggests that successfully balancing the budget requires focusing on the revenue side alongside expenditure control. He identifies collecting more tax from the gas industry as the easiest step to address ongoing budget deficits, which are forecast to continue well into the future.
summary: Rod Simms states that fossil fuel companies are effectively not paying for the natural resources their businesses depend on. He contends that collecting more tax from the gas industry is the easiest step to help address continuing budget deficits.
