title: LSU asks judge to dismiss SEC lawsuit over sovereign immunity
content: LSU is asking a federal judge to dismiss the SEC's lawsuit against the Tigers, arguing that many of the plaintiffs in the case are protected by sovereign immunity as state officials and that the league doesn't have jurisdiction.
summary: LSU is requesting a federal judge to dismiss the SEC's lawsuit against the Tigers. The university argues that the plaintiffs are protected by sovereign immunity and that the league lacks jurisdiction.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Indiana drops to No. 14 as Texas and Tennessee overtake Alabama in CFP rankings
content: Defending champion Indiana dropped six spots to No. 14 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings released Tuesday night. Meanwhile, Alabama fell out of the top five after being surpassed by Texas and Tennessee.
summary: Defending champion Indiana fell six spots to No. 14 in the latest CFP rankings released Tuesday night. Alabama fell out of the top five after Texas and Tennessee moved ahead of the Crimson Tide.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers to start Mason Rudolph against Broncos
content:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have benched four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers, who will be inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. The team announced that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback. This decision comes after the Steelers lost two consecutive games, dropping their record to 6-4, and occurred just days before Rodgers turns 43.

Notably, head coach Mike McCarthy had publicly backed Rodgers only a day prior to the benching decision. The Steelers confirmed the move in a statement released late Tuesday night.
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers announced that four-time MVP Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos. Quarterback Mason Rudolph will start in Rodgers' place as the team sits at 6-4 following two straight losses.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sandpapergate: Six burning questions remain unanswered in Australia ball tampering saga
content:
The Australian cricket ball tampering scandal, known as Sandpapergate, continues to generate controversy eight years after Cameron Bancroft was filmed holding sandpaper on a field in Cape Town. Although most individuals involved in the 2018 South Africa tour have publicly shared their accounts, not all details have been fully disclosed. The incident, described as a petty cricketing crime followed by a clumsy cover-up and a hurried investigation, resulted in penalties widely considered heavy for the main protagonists.

Despite the passage of time, the saga has become a persistent story within Australian cricket. As the scandal resurfaces with new and resurfaced allegations and counterclaims, the situation threatens to escalate into a civil war over the truth. The ongoing dispute highlights unresolved questions that keep the debate alive, challenging the finality of the original investigation and its outcomes.
summary: Most individuals involved in the 2018 South Africa tour have shared their accounts, but not every detail of the incident has been revealed. New and resurfaced allegations threaten to turn the fight for the truth into a civil war.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Cricket umpires discuss stress, social media, and technology in Wisden feature
content: Four umpires discuss how they deal with players, why they avoid social media, how technology is changing cricket and why umpiring beats being a football referee By Wisden Cricket Monthly Last summer, sat in a quiet ground at the fag-end of a four-dayer, with a few souls still kicking around and a clutch of cameras streaming what was left of the day live on YouTube, it struck me again what a great, strange sanctuary this place is, out there on the edges of the modern world. The game is trying to move, albeit at its own pace. Later that night, the day’s highlights would be landing on social media, available to all, for the game’s devotees to pore over and pick apart. More people are watching the County Championship than ever before. Streaming numbers show a growing audience in the UK and a widening uptake across the cricketing globe. The numbers aren’t yet earth-shattering, but how could they be, with such eccentric fare?
summary: Four cricket umpires discuss their methods for handling players, their avoidance of social media, and the impact of technology on the game. They also explain why they prefer umpiring cricket to refereeing football.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ronaldinho returns to Serie C after 11-year career hiatus
content:
The Knowledge has published a new installment of its Q&A segment, featuring a question from George Jones about footballers who have experienced extended career breaks. Jones notes that Ronaldinho recently made his first professional appearance in over 11 years while playing for Ravenna in Serie C. The article poses the central inquiry of whether any other players have endured a hiatus comparable to or longer than the 11-year gap.

The source details the specific circumstances surrounding Ronaldinho’s return. His previous professional match was on 26 September 2015, when he played for Fluminense in a 2-0 home victory against Goiás, a game in which he was substituted after 45 minutes. The piece highlights a notable symmetry in his return: 11 years and 50 days later, he played for Ravenna in a 2-0 home win against Forlì, also being withdrawn after 45 minutes. The article also briefly mentions other topics covered in the issue, including the fastest team to progress from FA Cup winners to the first round and matches delayed by snowball fights.
summary: Ronaldinho made his first professional appearance in over 11 years for Ravenna in Serie C, marking a return since his last match for Fluminense in 2015. The Brazilian was withdrawn after 45 minutes in the 2-0 home win against Forlì, mirroring his previous final appearance.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pelé and Maradona's first meeting arranged by reporter Guillermo Blanco in Rio, 1979
content:
A new book traces the early stages of the relationship between two of football’s greatest icons, beginning with a sunny afternoon in Rio de Janeiro in 1979. On that day, Pelé and Diego Maradona finally met after a series of aborted attempts to bring the two together.

Maradona had expressed to a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian legend. The meetings were delayed for several weeks, largely because Maradona did not want to travel on a Monday—a day he had free to spend with his girlfriend, Claudia. After a few weeks of failed attempts, the meeting was arranged in Rio.

Reporter Guillermo Blanco, writing for the Argentine sports magazine El Gráfico, secured permission from Pelé’s representatives and was determined to make the encounter happen. He checked Maradona onto a flight on a Sunday night without telling him, collared the young player after the Argentine Juniors played Huracán, then hurried to the airport. Maradona boarded the plane with his father, his agent, and a photographer, marking the first face‑to‑face meeting between the two stars.
summary: Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in Rio in April 1979 after Maradona led Argentina’s under‑20 side to the World Youth Cup final. Reporter Guillermo Blanco organized the meeting, secretly boarding Maradona on a Sunday night flight with his father, agent and a photographer after Argentine Juniors played Huracán.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Usman Khawaja sends proposed joint statement to Cricket Australia CEO over sandpaper crisis
content:
Usman Khawaja has revealed that he sent a proposed joint statement to Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg regarding the 2018 ball tampering incident in South Africa. Speaking on The Grade Cricketer podcast, the former Test opener outlined the text, which was intended for the entire 2018 Australian team to accept collective responsibility for the sandpaper crisis. Khawaja stated that the suggested wording has been put to Greenberg for consideration.

The proposed statement reads: “We accept knowledge as a team that we knew we were ball tampering by artificially altering the condition of the ball in South Africa in 2018.” Khawaja’s comments come amid calls for Cricket Australia to acknowledge that the team as a whole was aware of the ball tampering. Additionally, the former opener expressed disappointment regarding Pat Cummins’ recent press conference on the matter.
summary: Usman Khawaja proposed a joint statement for the 2018 Australia team to accept collective responsibility for ball tampering in South Africa. He has sent the wording to Todd Greenberg, Cricket Australia’s chief executive, for consideration.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Rangers win 3-2 over Aberdeen despite naivety and complacency, says McInnes
content: Rangers manager Derek McInnes admitted that his team’s naivety and complacency made their task harder, yet praised their resilience. The club secured a thrilling 3‑2 victory over Aberdeen, and McInnes highlighted the players’ ability to get the job done.
summary: Rangers manager Derek McInnes said the team's naivety and complacency made their task harder in a thrilling 3-2 win over Aberdeen. He praised the team's ability to get the job done.
author: BBC Sport

title: Newborn Hepatitis B Vaccination Rates Decline to 65.6% in 2026
content: A new study reports that the rate of newborns receiving the hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccine dropped to 65.6 percent in 2026, down from approximately 80 percent between 2020 and 2022. The decline is attributed to parents rejecting the immunization, which was once considered routine, following confusion associated with RFK Jr.
summary: A new study reports that the rate of newborns receiving the hepatitis B vaccine fell to 65.6% in 2026, down from about 80% between 2020 and 2022. The decline reflects increased parental rejection of the vaccine, which was once considered routine.
author: The Hill

title: Democrat opens investigation into Venezuela oil deal with reported tie to Vance
content: Senator Maggie Hassan, Democrat from New Hampshire, has demanded answers after a report alleged that Vice President Vance had a connection to a major energy company that received a license to sell Venezuelan oil shortly after the U.S. captured the country’s president. Hassan, the incoming chair of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, wrote a letter requesting information.
summary: Democrat opens investigation into Venezuela oil deal with reported tie to Vance.
author: The Hill

title: Scott Jennings urges Talarico, Colom to run for president
content: Political commentator Scott Jennings advised Democratic Senators-elect James Talarico of Texas and Scott Colom of Mississippi to run for president amid rising speculation about potential 2028 candidates. Jennings stated, “If I were Talarico or especially the guy in Mississippi, Colom … I would just go ahead and run for president,” offering his political consulting perspective on their prospects.
summary: Scott Jennings urges Talarico, Colom to run for president.
author: The Hill

title: Jim Cramer praises Nvidia CEO Huang's return after resignation amid affair reports
content: Jim Cramer reversed his earlier criticism of Jensen Huang when the former Nvidia chief was reinstated as CEO. Cramer, speaking on CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street” on Monday, noted that although Huang had resigned amid reports of extramarital affairs—including one with an alleged Chinese spy—he was now back in the role. “We may not like what he did, but he got off,” Cramer said.
summary: Jim Cramer praises Nvidia CEO Huang's return after resignation amid affair reports.
author: The Hill

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologizes to staff and says he attends daily therapy
content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to the company during his first all‑hands meeting with employees since being reinstated, admitting he has been in therapy every day, according to new reports. He said, “I made some terrible mistakes,” and added that he was unfaithful to his wife and had hurt his kids.
summary: Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, apologized to the company in his first all‑hands meeting with employees since being reinstated and said he is in therapy every day. He said he made terrible mistakes, including being unfaithful to his wife and hurting his kids.
author: The Hill

title: Sen. Van Hollen confirms Abrego Garcia self‑deported to Spain
content: Salvadoran migrant Kilmar Abrego Garcia, whose wrongful deportation sparked debate over President Trump’s immigration crackdown, self‑deported on Tuesday. Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D‑Md.) confirmed the move. ABC News reported that Abrego Garcia boarded a flight from a Washington, D.C.‑area airport to Madrid, Spain, as he faced deportation to one of several destinations.
summary: Salvadoran migrant Kilmar Abrego Garcia self‑deported to Madrid, Spain, after facing deportation. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D‑Md.) confirmed the departure, saying he would be safe.
author: The Hill

title: Trump to Meet Sen.-elect El‑Sayed About TrumpCare Rebranding
content: President Trump announced he will meet with Sen.-elect Abdul El‑Sayed (D‑Michigan) to discuss the rebranding of a single‑payer healthcare bill, formerly known as “Medicare for All,” as “TrumpCare.” In an interview with the New York Post, Trump praised El‑Sayed, calling him “very smart” and noting that the Michigan Democrat “did a good job.”
summary: Trump to Meet Sen.-elect El‑Sayed About TrumpCare Rebranding.
author: The Hill

title: Colom Says He’s Excited to Work with Trump at Itawamba County Town Hall
content:
Sen‑elect Scott Colom (D‑Miss.) hosted his first town hall in Fulton, Miss., after defeating incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde‑Smith (R‑Miss.). The event, streamed by Tupelo‑based outlet WTVA, brought constituents and community leaders together to discuss local concerns.  

During the forum, Colom said he was “excited” to work with President Trump on several issues, including healthcare.
summary: Colom Says He’s Excited to Work with Trump at Itawamba County Town Hall.
author: The Hill

title: Man and Dog Escaped King Tide on Oregon Beach, Video Released
content:
Cannon Beach police posted a video showing a man walking his dog on the beach on Tuesday when a sudden surge of tide swept both of them toward the water. The footage captured the man narrowly escaping the current, and authorities reported that both he and his dog made it back to dry land without injury.

The police department noted that the man had previously received a citation for driving on another beach and had been warned to stay away from the ocean because a “king tide” was expected that day. The warning came after the tide’s unusually high rise threatened to engulf the shoreline.

“King tides” is not a scientific term; they are exceptionally high tides that typically occur during a new or full moon when the moon is at its perigee. The department’s statement added that rising sea levels, combined with El Niño and king tides, are putting the U.S. west coast at high risk of record flooding. The report cited California’s recent stress tests of low‑lying areas in San Francisco and the broader threat of high tides and floods expected over Thanksgiving.
summary: Cannon Beach police posted footage of a man and his dog being swept by a king tide on a beach, but both returned to dry land uninjured. The man had earlier been cited for driving on another beach and was warned to stay away from the ocean as a king tide was expected.
author: Guardian Environment

title: George Monbiot: No sustainable way to eat fish, slams Marine Conservation Society guide
content:
George Monbiot argues that fishing is as harmful to marine ecosystems as tobacco is to human health. He dismisses claims from conservation charities that certain fish are safe to eat, stating that those recommendations do little to protect marine wildlife. Monbiot calls the idea of a single “sustainable” fish choice a myth.

In April, the Marine Conservation Society released its Good Fish Guide, urging consumers to stop eating cod and instead choose hake. The guide presented hake as a more environmentally friendly option. Monbiot notes that the Society later acknowledged that hake had become overexploited due to increased fishing pressure.

Six months after the initial recommendation, the Society downgraded hake’s sustainability rating. The change was attributed to the species’ overexploitation. Monbiot questions how such a shift occurred, implying a lack of consistent or reliable guidance from conservation groups.
summary: George Monbiot argues there is no sustainable way to eat fish and criticizes advice from conservation charities. He points out that the Marine Conservation Society’s Good Fish Guide first urged eating hake instead of cod, then six months later downgraded hake as overexploited.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Iowa Army Ammunition Plant to Detonate Lead Azide Stockpile Amid Public Concern
content:
The US Army plans to detonate the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday morning. This controlled blast, scheduled for the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, follows multiple delays and an outpouring of public concern regarding potential health and environmental impacts. The facility is located in a small town in south-eastern Iowa with a population of approximately 400.

The operation aims to dispose of 9,700lb (4,400kg) of the bomb-making chemical. Authorities warn that the explosion risks releasing plumes of toxic chemicals within a 100-mile (160km) radius. The specific location where these toxins may land remains uncertain as it shifts according to changing weather forecasts.
summary: The US Army will detonate the entire 9,700‑lb stockpile of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday morning, after multiple delays. The controlled blast could release toxic chemical plumes within a 100‑mile radius, sparking public concern about health and environmental effects.

title: HIV Viral Control Needed, but Not Enough for Healthy Aging
content: A recent report notes that individuals with HIV display accelerated biological aging. Blood‑based biomarkers reveal functions resembling older individuals rather than peers of the same chronological age. The findings underscore that controlling viral replication is necessary but alone does not ensure healthy aging.
summary: HIV viral control is necessary but not sufficient for healthy aging. Individuals with HIV exhibit signs of faster biological aging than people without HIV, with blood biomarkers resembling those of older individuals.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Methylmercury impairs forebrain inhibitory circuits and causes abnormal behavior in mice
content:
Global efforts to curb mercury pollution have not eliminated the threat posed by methylmercury (MeHg). The compound continues to persist in the environment, bioaccumulating along aquatic food chains. Humans mainly encounter MeHg through contaminated seafood. The devastating neurological effects of MeHg poisoning were first highlighted by Minamata disease, officially recognized in Japan in 1956. 

Since that time, researchers have examined MeHg’s neurotoxic impact, noting sensory, motor, and psychiatric symptoms. Although clinical reports document behavioral disturbances in affected individuals, the specific neural circuits responsible for these abnormalities remain poorly understood.
summary: Methylmercury impairs forebrain inhibitory circuits and induces abnormal behavior in mice. Clinical reports show behavioral disturbances in people exposed to MeHg, but the neural circuits responsible remain poorly understood.

title: Doctor reflects on US losing measles elimination status
content: A doctor reflects on the United States losing measles elimination status, noting that for many physicians of his generation, measles was rarely—or never—saw in practice. That was a sign of how well vaccination and public health efforts had worked.
summary: The doctor says many physicians of his generation rarely saw measles in practice. He says this rarity indicated successful vaccination and public health efforts.

title: FDA approves first new hormone therapy for early-stage breast cancer in over 20 years
content: The FDA has approved a new hormone therapy for early‑stage breast cancer, the first such approval in more than two decades. This marks a significant shift in treatment for the most common form of the disease.
summary: The FDA has approved a new hormone therapy for early-stage breast cancer. This is the first such approval in more than two decades.

title: Long‑term rise in fasting blood sugar linked to poorer midlife cognition
content: New independent research published in the Journal of the American Heart Association finds that young adults with progressive rises in fasting blood sugar over multiple decades were more likely to have worse cognitive health by midlife. Participants who developed type 2 diabetes during the study also showed signs of structural brain changes.
summary: Young adults who experienced a progressive rise in fasting blood sugar over multiple decades were more likely to have worse cognitive health by midlife. The study, published in the Journal of the American Heart Association, also found that participants who developed type 2 diabetes had signs of structural brain changes.

title: Single Vaping Episode Impairs Vascular Function, Study Finds
content: Researchers find a single vaping episode impairs vascular function, even when vaping without nicotine. The study’s results will be presented next week at the annual meeting of the Radiological Society of North America.
summary: Researchers found that a single vaping episode can negatively affect vascular function, even without nicotine. The study results will be presented next week at the RSNA annual meeting.

title: Feng Jian's team discovers cytokinin–NIN module driving spontaneous root nodules in alfalfa
content: A research team led by Professor Feng Jian of the Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology (IGDB) at the Chinese Academy of Sciences has identified a cytokinin–NODULE INCEPTION (NIN) regulatory module linked to spontaneous root nodule formation in alfalfa (Medicago sativa). This discovery explains how alfalfa can form nodules without rhizobia.
summary: Professor Feng Jian's research team at the Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology (IGDB) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences uncovered a cytokinin–NODULE INCEPTION (NIN) regulatory module linked to spontaneous root nodule formation in alfalfa. The discovery shows how alfalfa can form root nodules without rhizobia.

title: Ultrathin 'rainbow' sails could power spacecraft and shade the Earth
content:
Ultrathin “rainbow” sails have been proposed as a way to power spacecraft and shade the Earth. The idea builds on the physics of solar sailing, a concept that uses the momentum carried by photons in sunlight to generate a gentle push when the light bounces off a surface.

Solar sailing has gained renewed attention over the past decade, with several proof‑of‑concept flights demonstrating that the force from photons is sufficient to propel a spacecraft. These demonstrations confirm that the technology is feasible and could enable new forms of propulsion and planetary protection.
summary: Solar sailing uses the momentum of photons to push on surfaces, enabling propulsion. Proof‑of‑concept flights in the last decade have shown that solar sailing is indeed feasible.
author: Phys.org

title: 2026 Hurricane Season: El Niño Drives Record Pacific Storms, Calms Atlantic
content:
The 2026 hurricane season, ending Nov. 30, will be noted for stark contrasts between the Atlantic and Pacific, a classic sign of a very strong El Niño.

Atlantic activity was below normal, while Pacific activity was above average, including two disasters in Hawaii.
summary: The 2026 hurricane season, ending on Nov. 30, saw below‑normal activity across the Atlantic basin and above‑average activity in the Pacific, a classic sign of a very strong El Niño. The Pacific experienced two disasters in Hawaii.
author: Phys.org
